samples.summary: Gate 1b's CI_DEFINING_PATHS omits files ci.yml executes from the merge ref — `Dockerfile.playwright` is the whole browser lane, and a branch may edit it and still auto-promote
samples.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:528` runs `docker build -t wafflebase-playwright -f Dockerfile.playwright .` and `:533` runs that image as the entire `verify-browser (22.x)` lane. Both come from the PR MERGE REF, exactly like `ci.yml` itself. `Dockerfile.playwright` is not matched by any entry in `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:123-135), so `definesCi("Dockerfile.playwright")` is false and `ranBaseCiDefinition` (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:222) returns true. A branch whose Dockerfile CMD is `true` produces a genuinely green CI run at the genuine path, gate 1 passes, gate 1b passes, and mark-ready posts the hand-off comment that now asserts "the CI definition that run executed came from `main`" (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:382-388). The same holds for `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` and `packages/design-sandbox/vitest.config.ts`, which choose which tests vitest collects for those lanes. The fix belongs on the new code: add these paths to CI_DEFINING_PATHS (and, since checks.test.mjs asserts the mirror is a superset of `harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig`, the extra entries are already permitted there). Note the doc's admitted residue is "a branch can weaken its own tests"; a Dockerfile that defines the lane's entrypoint is not test content, so this is inside the claim the gate makes, not the residue it disclaims.
searchedFor: grep for CI_DEFINING_PATHS / definesCi consumers repo-wide

samples.summary: set-state.mjs is now the only check-run reader left without the producer filter this change makes mandatory for gate 2
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:240-242` still selects lens runs by NAME alone: `checks.filter((c) => (c.name || "").startsWith("agent-review-"))`, then derives `reviewChecksPresent` / `lensBlocked` from them. Every other reader in the repo applies the producer check the diff has now added to `checkPassed`: `rounds.mjs:200,230,585`, `review-round-guard.mjs:222`, `review-state.mjs:144`, `loop-status.mjs:193`, `fix-brief.mjs:101`, `fix-eligible.mjs:55`. After this change the comment on `CHECK_PRODUCER_APP_SLUG` (checks.mjs:254) claims those modules 'already take' this posture and that 'gate 2 was the one reader that did not' — set-state is a second one it does not name. Impact is bounded: the agent:* label is advisory, not a gate, so a check run named `agent-review-x` from any installed App can only mislabel a PR `agent:blocked` (or make it look reviewed), not promote it. Left as-is it will drift from the invariant the diff just established.

samples.summary: New CHECK_PRODUCER_APP_SLUG export duplicates eight existing hard-coded "github-actions" literals that were not switched to it
samples.evidence: The diff introduces `export const CHECK_PRODUCER_APP_SLUG = "github-actions"` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:257) but every pre-existing producer check still spells the literal: `fix-brief.mjs:101`, `fix-eligible.mjs:55`, `review-state.mjs:144`, `rounds.mjs:200`, `rounds.mjs:230`, `rounds.mjs:585`, `review-round-guard.mjs:222`, `loop-status.mjs:193`. There are now nine definitions of one trust decision; changing the trusted producer (e.g. moving the panel to its own App installation) would silently update gate 2 and leave the other eight believing the old slug — the readers would then disagree about which check runs are evidence. Nothing is broken today; the fix is to import the constant at those sites.

samples.summary: verify-self.mjs's own sibling imports are outside CI_DEFINING_PATHS, so gate 1b's "the branch supplied no part of the CI/harness definition" claim is wider than the list backing it
samples.evidence: `scripts/verify-self.mjs:2-3` imports `./failure-summary.mjs` and `./agent/git-env.mjs`. `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` covers `scripts/verify-*.mjs` and `scripts/changed-areas.mjs` but neither of those two, so a PR editing them passes gate 1b while changing code the verify lane actually executes from the merge ref. Lower impact than the lane-definition gap above (these modules format failure output and read the head SHA, so the plausible failure mode is a red run rather than a false green), but the gate's stated claim in scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:20-24 does not carve them out. Fix belongs on the new list in checks.mjs — or on the prose, narrowing the claim.

samples.summary: design-pr.mjs can open PRs against a non-default base, which the new gate 1b refuses outright rather than measuring
samples.evidence: `scripts/design-pr.mjs:385` builds `['pr','create', …, '--base', value('base') ?? 'main']`, i.e. a caller may target any base. mark-ready's new gate 1b (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:239-244) throws — and therefore fails the gate — for any PR whose `baseRefName` is not the repository default branch, so such a PR can never be auto-promoted and will sit as a draft until a human flips it. That is the documented intent of the base-pinning, but this is the one call site in the repo that can produce such a PR, and it is not aware of the new precondition. Worth a note in design-pr.mjs (or accepting that stacked/non-main PRs are human-promoted by design).
searchedFor: grep for other mark-ready invocations (only agent-review-panel.yml:1508)

verdict.reason: No counterexample exists. CI_DEFINING_PATHS (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:123-135) contains no Dockerfile entry and its glob compiler anchors both ends with non-separator-crossing `*` (checks.mjs:140-159), so definesCi("Dockerfile.playwright") is false; harness.config.json:52-62's ciConfig also omits it, and the mirror test's positive list (checks.test.mjs:516-532) confirms the covered surface. Meanwhile ci.yml:526-537 builds and runs Dockerfile.playwright with no command override, so Dockerfile.playwright:7's CMD (`node ./scripts/verify-browser-lanes.mjs`) IS the whole verify-browser lane, executed from the merge ref (checkout ci.yml:509); a branch editing that CMD is an unmapped path, which forces full/heavy (changed-areas.test.mjs:204-209), so the gutted lane really runs and concludes green. mark-ready.mjs:193-214/298-303 shows gate 1b's only path test is definesCi and no other gate is path-based; repo-wide grep for CI_DEFINING_PATHS/definesCi finds mark-ready as the sole consumer, and repo-wide grep for `Dockerfile` finds no guard on the promote path. The hand-off comment (mark-ready.mjs:382-389) therefore asserts "the CI definition that run executed came from main" while disclaiming only weakened test content — a lane entrypoint is not that residue. In-lane for blast-radius: a new guard with a reachable second entry point that reaches the protected outcome without passing through it.

searchedFor: read docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1981-1994 (the enumeration of which consumers need the clause)
finding.summary: The new `workflow_run.path` guard is applied to the three CI consumers but NOT to capture-collect.yml, which consumes `workflow_run` by DISPLAY NAME ("Agent Review Panel" / "Agent Review On-Demand") with no path, branch or head-repository clause — and it checks out another repository with `secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN` and pushes to it.
finding.evidence: .github/workflows/capture-collect.yml:67-69 `workflow_run: workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"] types: [completed]`; the only job gate is line 129 `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'skipped'` — no `path`, no `head_repository`, no branch restriction. Lines 142-146 then check out `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `token: ${{ secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN }}` and the collector later pushes. The exact forgery the diff closes elsewhere (a second workflow file claiming a display name, pushable by anyone with workflows write on the base repo — the `agent:managed` human-PR threat model this change cites) reaches this consumer unchanged, and unlike docker-publish/publish-ghpage it is reachable from a PR branch because there is no `head_branch == 'main'` clause. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1987-1990 enumerates the exempt consumers and never mentions capture-collect.yml, so it looks overlooked rather than deliberately excluded. Fix belongs on capture-collect.yml (add a `github.event.workflow_run.path` clause for the two producer files) or on the doc if the exposure is accepted.

verdict.reason: The finding's decisive claim — that the design doc "enumerates the exempt consumers and never mentions capture-collect.yml, so it looks overlooked" — is false. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2045-2059, in the same section as the enumeration at 2038-2043, names capture-collect.yml explicitly as "the same class and NOT yet guarded — an open gap, recorded here rather than implied away", states the identical threat (a second file calling itself "Agent Review Panel"), the identical one-line `workflow_run.path` remedy against the two producer files, why the blast radius is bounded, and why the change cannot carry it (the agent App has no `workflows` scope). The finding's own accepted alternative fix ("or on the doc if the exposure is accepted") is therefore already in the tree. I independently verified the bounding facts rather than trusting the doc: capture-collect.yml:101-103 is read-only permissions; collect-captures.test.mjs:1248-1273 pins that no `ref:` and no head_sha/head_branch/head_ref/pull_requests may appear, so a forged trigger cannot execute branch content in the token-holding job; capture-collect.yml:156-160,191-194 show collection is a fixed 7-day window, not trigger-derived, so the forged payload influences nothing (and the nightly schedule at line 74-75 would collect the same artifacts anyway, meaning the proposed clause would not close the artifact path). It is also not a bypass of the guard this change adds: capture-collect consumes the two panels, not "CI", so a forged `name: CI` run never reaches it.
